spec.assertion: Tracer-counted heals reaching crown must exceed 40 AND 3x the full-burst count (~100 expected: RL 6 rounds / 60f charge / 159f reload). RED under fullBurstEnter (~9), burstCast (<=3), interval 15s (12); the FB_TRIGGER counterfactual run demonstrates the collapse.

helm (4th slot, outside the engine's leftmost-`count` stand-in for lowest-HP) receives fewer than a quarter of crown's rapunzel-sourced recoveries. RED under an all-allies target (helm === crown) and under a 4+-ally count.
it.skip — the engine models no HP pool and the heal effect carries no amount field, so the magnitude has no observable. Only the recovery-trigger emission is testable (covered above).

Exactly 2 distinct targetSlugs receive a rapunzel-cast maxHpFlat buffApply, and helm (the only Attacker-class unit, top final ATK under static and live ranking) is one of them. RED under an all-allies model (4 targets), a self-only model (1), and an alliesLowestAtk model (helm absent).

Emitted as maxHpFlat (caster-scaled stats flat-resolve at apply) and damage-inert: stripping skill2 leaves every unit's total byte-identical, pinning the e3 rule that ally-granted Max HP feeds no teammate ATK conversion. RED if the line were mis-encoded onto any damage-bearing stat.
it.skip — no incoming-healing StatKey exists and there is no HP pool for it to scale. Guarded negatively by the kit-wide inertness test (it must not surface as an offensive stat).

Structural: the burst-slot heal block triggers on burstCast (not fullBurstEnter) and targets allies without excludeSelf. Asserted structurally because rapunzel is Burst I sharing the slot with liter (20s CD) and may never cast in the control comp; behaviourally the helm inequality still holds at 0-3 casts.
it.skip — no HP pool, no incapacitation state, nobody ever dies against the immortal partless boss; the target set is unreachable by construction.

it.skip — the HP-threshold trigger is unmodellable (no HP pool) and resolveTargets({kind:'enemy'}) returns no entity. Guarded by a structural assertion that any stun effect in the kit is enemy-targeted, so a mis-modelled stun can never halt an ally's fire/charge/reload.

No rapunzel-cast buffApply carries any of the 31 damage-bearing StatKeys. RED if any heal/Max-HP/incoming-healing line were over-modelled into an ATK/crit/damage-up stat to make a support unit 'do something'.

fixtures: controlComp('rapunzel', true) only — liter B1 / crown B2 / rapunzel / helm B3, boss Fire, focus rapunzel. Five hoisted 180s runs: CLEAN (untouched, the inertness reference), BASE (shipped kit + tracers), NO_HEAL (all heal effects stripped — the other-healer baseline that the deltas subtract out), FB_TRIGGER (skill1 heal re-keyed to fullBurstEnter — the nearest-wrong trigger), NO_SKILL2 (skill2 blocks removed). Because the engine emits no heal event, heals are instrumented by pushing a recovery-triggered inert partsDamagePct buff onto crown's and helm's in-memory overrides (unique tracer value, counted by targetSlug), plus a passive self tracer on rapunzel to recover her caster index; the first test proves both tracers are damage-neutral by asserting BASE totals equal CLEAN totals. The fixed-B3 helm slot is KEPT deliberately: she is the 4th ally (target-set discriminator) and the only Attacker-class unit (highest-final-ATK discriminator).
gaps: skill1 'Recovers 4.03% of the skill user's final Max HP as HP' — no HP pool in v1; the heal effect models no amount, only the recovery emission.
skill2 'Incoming healing ▲13.65% for 15 sec' — no incoming-healing StatKey; nothing in v1 consumes healing magnitude.
burst 'Resurrect 1 incapacitated highest-final-ATK ally with 81.67% HP' — no HP pool, no incapacitation state; the target set can never be non-empty.
burst 'Activates when HP falls below 30%. Affects all enemies. Stun for 1 sec' — HP-threshold trigger unmodellable and the enemy target resolves to no entity (the stun primitive is unit-facing).

skill2 duration semantics ('for 15 sec' with no activation clause) — passive-always-on and interval+durationSec:15 are observationally identical here (no HP consumer), so the test asserts target set + inertness rather than binding one encoding.
